title: Proximity-aware column throttling and ARIA delta announcements for virtualized table
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Our virtualized table performs well for large datasets but currently has jarring column-resize behavior and no concise accessibility feedback when columns are added/removed or density changes happen. Small pointer drifts cause large layout jumps because the runtime snaps multiple columns at once. Goal: Design a subtle, predictable UX that prevents jumbo jumps during drag/resize, lets users tune density per-column, and surfaces a compact ARIA delta announcement (what changed) for screen-reader users instead of re-reading entire row contents. This ticket scopes the design exploration, interaction spec, and acceptance criteria for handoff to engineering. We will focus on: 1) Proximity-aware column throttling (throttle resize updates to the most-impacted column and adjacent gutters to reduce reflow), 2) Per-column density override UI in column header menu (small/compact/expanded), 3) Non-intrusive ARIA delta announcement pattern that announces: "Column X width updated to Y" and "Column Y density changed to compact" with minimal verbosity, 4) Edge cases: frozen columns, column groups, and keyboard resize paths.
acceptance_criteria: When dragging a column edge, only the actively dragged column and its immediate neighbor update layout on each animation frame; other columns maintain stable widths until the user releases (prevents layout storms).
Column header context menu exposes a density selector (Compact / Default / Spacious) that applies per-column without breaking virtualization or row height measurement.
Screen-reader announcement uses an ARIA "delta" live region that phrases updates succinctly (examples provided) and respects user's reduced-motion and verbosity preferences.
Keyboard resize: using modifier+arrow keys resizes in single-pixel steps with an announcement after the interaction completes (on blur or Enter).
Design tokens for density (rowPaddingCompact, rowPaddingDefault, rowPaddingSpacious) mapped to existing tokens and documented in the design system guidelines.
design_notes: Proximity-aware throttling: recommend 60Hz UI updates but only compute reflow for the active column and +/-1 neighbor. For large tables, defer batch width recalculation until dragend (with visually plausible placeholders).
Use a visual micro-handle: 8px grab zone but 2px visible gutter; this reduces pointer jitter. Add subtle drag shadow to indicate active column. Keep contrast to token standards.
Density selector lives in header overflow menu; avoid increasing header height. Persist per-user via storage hook but expose reset to table defaults in table-level menu.

ARIA approach: single polite live region with delta messages. Message templates: 'Column "{label}" width set to {width}px' and 'Column "{label}" density set to {densityLabel}'. Avoid announcing cell content to prevent verbosity.
decisions: Will implement density tokens rather than ad-hoc CSS values so that spacing can be reused by other components.
Throttling -> favor UX fluidity over millimetric precision; rounding widths to nearest 2px during drag to reduce layout churn.
ARIA live region approach chosen over per-cell aria-label updates to keep SR verbosity low and implementation simpler for engineering.
tradeoffs: Deferring full reflow until dragend reduces immediate visual correctness for a small subset of columns but dramatically improves frame rate for huge tables.
Per-column density increases complexity for height measurement; we accept a small added cost in virtualization measurement in exchange for user control.
comments: 2026-03-02 Ava Chen: Created ticket after pairing with frontend on observed flicker during high-frequency resize on large datasets. Initial prototype attached in Figma and Loom. Requested accessibility review early.

2026-03-04 Sofia Martinez: Ran 3 quick unmoderated tests with PMs. Users liked smaller visible grabs and per-column density control; they were confused by immediately changing many columns during a drag. Proposed proximity throttling exploration.

2026-03-06 Accessibility (Rohan Patel): Reviewed ARIA draft. Suggested using a single polite live region and avoiding assertive announcements to not disrupt screen-reader navigation. Also suggested tying announcements to user preference for verbosity.

2026-03-08 Frontend (Maya Rivera): Engineering notes — can implement throttling in the UI layer and emit a single synthetic resize event on dragend to reconcile sizes. Concern: per-column density requires virtualized measurement hook changes (ENG-3121).
2026-03-10 Ava Chen: Updated designs to include micro-handle and density chooser mockups. Added token names and mapping table in the Confluence doc. Ready for handoff to ENG-3121 in next sprint.

2026-03-12 Sofia Martinez: Placed in 'In Progress' and added estimate 3. Blocking: ENG-3121 acceptance tests for virtualization-measure API. Next: finalize copy for ARIA messages and QA script for SR testing.
